t: 3557 – Find Maximum Number of Non Intersecting Substrings
o: Count the maximum number of disjoint substrings of length ≥ 4 that start and end with the same letter. Greedy works: scanning left to right, whenever the current character c appeared before at position p with i − p ≥ 3 (giving length ≥ 4) and p lies after the end of the last chosen substring, take the substring [p, i] — taking the earliest-ending valid candidate is optimal (classic interval scheduling exchange argument). Update the last-seen position of c afterwards. Example 1: 'a' at 0 and 5 → take [0,5]; 'f' at 6 and 9 → take [6,9] → 2.
k: A valid substring for letter c is any pair of c-occurrences ≥ 3 apart; the earliest-ending one per step is greedily safe.
Track last occurrence per letter and the right end of the last selected substring.

a.i: For each index i, if word[i] previously occurred at p, i−p ≥ 3, and p > lastEnd, select this substring (count++, lastEnd=i). Always refresh last[word[i]]=i so future candidates start after i.
s: At each i, attempt to close a substring with the stored previous occurrence.
a.t: O(n) — single pass with O(1) map operations.

w: Why greedy is optimal: any solution can swap its earliest-finishing substring for the greedy pick without reducing the count (exchange argument). Pitfall: update last[c] even when a substring was taken, so the next candidate starts strictly after lastEnd. Follow-up: the Hard version asks for the maximum total LENGTH of such substrings, needing a different DP.
